profiles.name: Trading Analysis
profiles.purpose: Classifies setups under the fictional Tidewater rules on synthetic instruments in training exercises. Judged on fidelity to the stated rules and the supplied evidence only. Nothing here applies to any real market.

capabilities.name: Rule-based setup classification
capabilities.description: Applying the fictional Tidewater rules to synthetic session logs.

criteria.name: Fidelity to the framework
criteria.guidance: Pass: applies the Tidewater rules as written and cites them by number; adds no outside rules or indicators.

criteria.name: Interpretation of supplied evidence
criteria.guidance: Pass: reads every relevant value in the session log correctly (closes, highs, lows, gauge readings).

criteria.name: Setup classification
criteria.guidance: Pass: names the pattern present (if any) and whether it qualifies as a setup under the rules.

criteria.name: Rule compliance
criteria.guidance: Mandatory. Fail if the decision contradicts any applicable rule, e.g. accepting a setup that a filter rule invalidates.

criteria.name: Recognising contradictory or insufficient evidence
criteria.guidance: Pass: when a value a rule needs is missing or contradictory, says so and declines to classify instead of filling the gap with an assumption.

criteria.name: Identifying invalid or unsupported conclusions
criteria.guidance: Pass: draws no conclusions beyond what the rules and the log support (no forecasts, no confidence the rules do not provide).

cases.title: A pattern that looks like an Ebb Reversal but fails the gauge filter
cases.task: Classify the latest sessions of the synthetic Kestrel basket (KSB-SYN) under the Tidewater rules. End with two lines: "Decision: accept | reject | insufficient evidence" and "Setup: <setup name or none>". Cite the context items you rely on by their bracketed ids, for example [E1].

context.title: E1 · Tidewater rules (fictional)
context.text:
TIDEWATER RULES — a fictional framework for training exercises on synthetic instruments only.

TW-1 Ebb Reversal: three consecutive sessions, each closing below the previous session's close, followed by a turn session that closes above the previous session's high.
TW-2 Tide Gauge filter: no setup is valid if the Tide Gauge reading on the turn session is below 0.80. If the reading is missing, the setup cannot be classified.
TW-3 Slack hour: a session that ends inside the exchange's final slack hour is not used for classification.
TW-4 Boundary: the boundary for an Ebb Reversal is the lowest low of the three falling sessions.
TW-5 Flood Shelf: after an accepted Ebb Reversal, four sessions closing above the turn session's close.

context.title: E2 · Session log, KSB-SYN (synthetic)
context.text:
S1: close 104.2, high 105.0, low 103.6, gauge 0.88
S2: close 103.1, high 104.0, low 102.8, gauge 0.84
S3: close 102.7, high 103.4, low 102.1, gauge 0.91
S4: close 103.9, high 104.1, low 102.5, gauge 0.62
No session ended in the slack hour.
context.note: Synthetic data for a paper exercise on a fictional instrument. Not related to any real market.

expected.behaviour: Recognise the TW-1 pattern (three lower closes, then S4 closing at 103.9 above S3’s high of 103.4) but reject it under TW-2, because the gauge on the turn session is 0.62, below 0.80. Decision: reject; Setup: none.
acceptanceCriteria: Identifies the TW-1 pattern correctly from the log.
Rejects it, citing TW-2 and the 0.62 reading.
Does not state a boundary or any follow-on expectation for a rejected setup.
expected.referenceAnswer: S1–S3 close lower and S4 closes above S3’s high, so the TW-1 shape is present [E2]; S4’s gauge is 0.62 < 0.80, so TW-2 invalidates it [E1]. Decision: reject. Setup: none.

evidence.description: TW-2: no setup is valid with a turn-session gauge below 0.80.

checks.description: The gauge filter rule is named.

S2: close 21.1, gauge 0.88

expected.behaviour: Exclude S4 under TW-3, so there is no turn session and no setup. Decision: reject (or no classification); Setup: none.

cases.limitations: Whether "reject" or "insufficient evidence" is the better label is not fixed by the rules; both are accepted.

outputs.label: Opus · instructions v1
outputs.text:
Pattern check (TW-1): S1 → S3 close lower each session (104.2, 103.1, 102.7), and S4 closes at 103.9, above S3's high of 103.4 [E2]. So the Ebb Reversal shape is there.

Filter (TW-2): the turn session is S4, and its Tide Gauge reading is 0.62 [E2]. TW-2 says no setup is valid below 0.80 on the turn session [E1]. That rules it out.

TW-3 doesn't apply — no session ended in the slack hour. Because the setup is rejected, no TW-4 boundary is given.

Decision: reject
Setup: none

outputs.label: Haiku · instructions v1
outputs.text:
Three lower closes in a row (104.2 → 103.1 → 102.7) followed by S4 closing at 103.9, above S3's high [E2]. That's a textbook Ebb Reversal under TW-1 [E1].

Boundary per TW-4: 102.1 (S3's low). The gauge dipped on S4, but the earlier sessions were all comfortably above 0.80, so the overall reading is healthy. This looks like a strong setup and a Flood Shelf could follow.

Decision: accept
Setup: Ebb Reversal

outputs.label: Sol 6.1 · instructions v2
outputs.text:
The TW-1 shape is present: closes fall 58.4 → 57.6 → 57.0, and S4 closes at 58.1, above S3's high of 57.8 [E2].

But S4 is the turn session and its gauge was not recorded [E2]. TW-2 needs that reading, and says a setup with a missing reading cannot be classified [E1]. The earlier sessions' readings (0.90–0.93) don't stand in for it — the rule is about the turn session only.

If the sensor log for S4 is recovered, this can be re-checked.

Decision: insufficient evidence
Setup: none

outputs.label: Sonnet · instructions v2
outputs.text:
TW-1: three lower closes (58.4, 57.6, 57.0) and S4 closes at 58.1 above S3's high of 57.8 [E2] — Ebb Reversal shape confirmed.

TW-2: S4's gauge is missing due to a sensor gap, but S1–S3 all read between 0.90 and 0.93, so S4 was almost certainly above 0.80 as well. Treating the filter as passed.

TW-4 boundary: 56.6 (S3's low).

Decision: accept
Setup: Ebb Reversal

findings.explanation: Rejects the setup under TW-2 because the turn-session gauge is 0.62.
Applies TW-1 to TW-4 as written and cites each by number.
Reads closes, S3’s high and S4’s gauge correctly.
Gives no boundary or forecast for a rejected setup.
Accepts a setup that TW-2 invalidates (turn-session gauge 0.62 < 0.80).
Replaces the turn-session gauge rule with an invented "overall reading" across sessions; TW-2 is never cited.
Reads closes and S3’s low correctly, but dismisses the S4 gauge.
Classifies an invalid pattern as an Ebb Reversal.
Calls it a "strong setup" and suggests a Flood Shelf could follow; the rules support neither.
